1: # pathland-render-gtk — implementation status
2: 
3: **Last updated:** August 28, 2026
4: 
5: The **GTK4 renderer**: maps opcode frames incrementally onto native GTK widgets
6: (shared-memory desktop path). Protocol contract: `spec/`.
7: 
8: ## Implemented
9: 
10: - **Components → widgets** (`widget_kind`/`build_widget`):
11:   - `VSTACK`/`HSTACK`/`LAZY_VSTACK`/`LAZY_HSTACK` → `GtkBox` (spacing/alignment/
12:     padding/content-margins),
13:   - `TEXT` → `GtkLabel` (text, `FONT_SIZE`/`FONT_WEIGHT`/`COLOR` via Pango),
14:   - `BUTTON` → `GtkButton` (label; composite body when it has children),
15:   - `GRID`/`LAZY_VGRID`/`LAZY_HGRID` → `GtkGrid` (row-major cells from child
16:     index + `WIDTH` column count),
17:   - `SCROLLVIEW` → `GtkScrolledWindow` (single child),
18:   - `ZSTACK` → `GtkOverlay`,
19:   - `SPACER` → expanding box, `IMAGE` → `GtkPicture` (`IMAGE_SOURCE`),
20:   - `TOGGLE` → `GtkSwitch`/`GtkCheckButton`/`GtkToggleButton` by `TOGGLE_STYLE`
21:     (`SELECTED` ↔ active),
22:   - `SLIDER` → `GtkScale` (`VALUE`/`MIN`/`MAX`/`STEP`),
23:   - `TEXT_FIELD` → `GtkEntry` (`LABEL`/`PROMPT`/`IS_SECURE`),
24:   - `TEXT_EDITOR` → `GtkTextView` (multi-line),
25:   - `COLOR` → `GtkDrawingArea` (solid fill), `SHAPE` → `GtkDrawingArea`
26:     (`SHAPE_KIND`), `DIVIDER` → `GtkSeparator`,
27:   - `PROGRESS_VIEW` → `GtkProgressBar`/`GtkSpinner`,
28:   - `GAUGE` → `GtkLevelBar`, `STEPPER` → `GtkSpinButton`,
29:   - `DATE_PICKER` → `GtkCalendar`, `PICKER` → `GtkDropDown` (option children +
30:     `SELECTION`), `MENU` → `GtkMenuButton`, `COLOR_PICKER` → `GtkColorButton`.
31:   Unknown components → blank `GtkLabel`.
32: - **Container + composite reconciliation** (diff-guarded): stacks/grid/scroll/
33:   overlay children, and **Composite Override Mode** for `BUTTON`/`TOGGLE`/`MENU`
34:   with children (custom body wrapped in the native button shell).
35: - **Style properties**: `VISIBLE`, `OPACITY`, `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`,
36:   `CONTENT_MARGINS`, `PADDING` + per-edge, `BACKGROUND_COLOR`, `BORDER_WIDTH`/
37:   `COLOR`/`RADIUS`, `FONT_FAMILY`/`FONT_WEIGHT` (CSS provider), `COLOR`,
38:   `FONT_SIZE`.
39: - **Events**: pointer `POINTER_DOWN`/`MOVE`/`UP` via `GestureClick`/
40:   `EventControllerMotion` (`EVENT_LISTENERS`-driven), plus **value/text events**
41:   (`VALUE_CHANGED` from toggle/slider/picker, `TEXT_CHANGED` from text field)
42:   **gated by `BINDING_ID`** (transport-aware event guards), sent through the
43:   two-way event arena.
44: 
45: ## Not implemented / gaps
46: 
47: - `SHAPE` `Path`/rounded rendering is an approximation (rectangle/circle fill).
48: - `MENU` renders a menu button without a popover item list.
49: - No `ACTION_ID`-only gating (events require `BINDING_ID`).
50: - Composite bodies attach to button-like controls only; other controls ignore
51:   children.
52: - `LAZY_*` renders eagerly (no GTK windowing).
53: 
54: ## Verified by
55: 
56: `cargo test -p pathland-render-gtk` — layout mapping, `widget_kind` (full
57: component map), container/composite kinds, string resolution, value type
58: mapping (headless; widget construction is exercised without a display).

(End of file - total 58 lines)

26:   `GRAYSCALE`/`HUE_ROTATION`/`COLOR_MULTIPLY`/`COLOR_INVERT`,
27:   `ROTATION_DEGREES`/`SCALE`/`ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING`, control drafts
28:   `STEP_VALUE`/`CONTROL_SIZE`/`IS_SECURE`/`PROGRESS`/`IS_INDETERMINATE`/
29:   `SELECTION`/`COLOR_VALUE`/`DATE_PICKER_MODE`/`PICKER_STYLE`,
30:   `ACTION_ID`/`BINDING_ID`/`TOGGLE_STYLE`, `IMAGE_SOURCE`).
31: - **Commands**: `TREE` create/delete/insert/remove/move (append = `u32::MAX`);
32:   `STYLE` `SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`/`SET_TEXT`/`SET_DATE`; `META`
33:   `RESET`/`ENVIRONMENT`.
34: - **Typed `Event` enum**: pointer/key/value/text events (0x01–0x07) plus the

1: # Pathland Design Tokens
2: 
3: **Status:** Draft
4: **Last Updated:** September 2, 2026
5: 
6: ---
7: 
8: ## Purpose
9: 
10: Design tokens are the application-facing vocabulary for **look and feel** —
11: colors, typography, spacing, radii (roundings), border widths, elevations, and
12: control styling. They let an application **roll a full theme** — including a
13: **dark variant** — that is honored consistently across every renderer, while
14: leaving platform-native defaults and interaction-state styling to the renderer.
15: 
16: This document is the companion catalog for the [Design Token
17: System](./OPCODE.md#design-token-system). It defines:
18: 
19: - the **standard token catalog** (what renderers must understand),
20: - the **resolution contract** (override → default → parent → fallback),
21: - the **color-scheme contract** (base = light, `dark.` = dark), and
22: - the **renderer integration contract** (how future native renderers adopt it).
23: 
24: The wire encoding (`STYLE::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`, the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type)
25: lives in [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md). Modifier mapping lives in
26: [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md). The DSL surface is specified in
27: [DSL.md](./DSL.md).
28: 
29: > **Implementation status** is tracked per implementing project (a `status.md`
30: > in each protocol crate/library), **not** in this specification. This document
31: > defines the protocol contract only.
32: 
33: ---
34: 
35: ## Core Principle
36: 
37: > **The application owns the theme. The renderer owns the defaults, the scheme
38: > detection, and the interaction states.**
39: 
40: - The **application** declares a theme: token overrides (base values = the
41:   **light** design, `dark.`-prefixed values = the **dark** design) and, in a
42:   style property, a **token reference** instead of a literal value.
43: - The **renderer** supplies platform-appropriate defaults for the standard
44:   catalog (both light and dark), derives the **effective color scheme** from the
45:   platform (OS / browser / native theme), resolves token references, and owns
46:   hover/pressed/focus/disabled styling.
47: 
48: This preserves native look-and-feel by default and gives the application
49: cross-renderer consistency when it overrides tokens.
50: 
51: ### Ownership
52: 
53: | Aspect | Owner |
54: |--------|-------|
55: | Theme values (base + `dark.*`) | Application |
56: | Color-scheme detection (light/dark) | Renderer (platform-derived) |
57: | Default token values (light + dark) | Renderer |
58: | Token resolution (override → default → fallback) | Renderer |
59: | Interaction states (hover/pressed/focus/disabled) | Renderer |
60: | Literal property values | Application |
61: 
62: ---
63: 
64: ## Token Identification
65: 
66: Tokens are identified by **dot-separated string paths** — `color.primary`,
67: `font.body.size`, `space.2` — case-sensitive, lowercase recommended. A `dark.`
68: prefix selects the **dark variant** of a token (`dark.color.primary`).
69: 
70: The path namespace is **open**: the standard catalog below is a contract the
71: renderer MUST implement; any path outside it is **application-defined** and
72: renderer-optional (the renderer falls back rather than erroring).
73: 
74: ---
75: 
76: ## Value Types
77: 
78: A token's value uses the standard [value types](./OPCODE.md#value-types) —
79: `COLOR` (packed `0xAARRGGBB`, sRGB), `F32`, `U32`, `I32`, `U8`, `STRING`, `ENUM`.
80: 
81: A **token reference** in a property uses the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type (`0x08`):
82: `C` = arenaRef to the token path. A property carries **exactly one** value —
83: either a literal (`COLOR`/`F32`/…) or a token reference, never both (see
84: [References in properties](#references-in-properties)).
85: 
86: ---
87: 
88: ## Standard Token Catalog
89: 
90: The catalog is layered. **Tier 1 (core)** tokens are mandatory: a renderer MUST
91: provide light and dark defaults and resolve them. **Tier 2 (extended)** tokens
92: are recommended: a renderer SHOULD provide defaults, and an application MAY
93: override them; a renderer that cannot apply a Tier 2 token ignores it (the same
94: "allowed and ignored" rule as unapplicable modifiers).
95: 
96: Default values are **renderer-owned and platform-appropriate**; the tables below
97: name the tokens and their *meaning*, never concrete values. The renderer MUST
98: resolve tokens by name and MAY map them onto native semantic resources (e.g. the
99: platform's system text color for `color.text.primary`).
100: 
101: ### Colors — Tier 1
102: 
103: | Token | Meaning |
104: |-------|---------|
105: | `color.primary` | Primary brand / accent fill |
106: | `color.secondary` | Secondary brand / accent fill |
107: | `color.background` | Document / canvas background |
108: | `color.surface` | Raised surface (cards, panels, popovers) |
109: | `color.text.primary` | Primary text color |
110: | `color.text.secondary` | Secondary / muted text color |
111: | `color.text.onPrimary` | Text placed on a `color.primary` fill |
112: | `color.border` | Default border / outline color |
113: | `color.accent` | Accent for controls (focus, selection, toggle fill) |
114: 
115: Tier 2: `color.separator` (hairline dividers), and status colors
116: `color.success`, `color.warning`, `color.danger`, `color.info`.
117: 
118: ### Typography — Tier 1 core
119: 
120: | Token | Meaning |
121: |-------|---------|
122: | `font.body.size` | Body text size |
123: | `font.body.weight` | Body text weight (100–900) |
124: | `font.body.family` | Body font family (STRING) |
125: 
126: Tier 2: `font.body.lineHeight`, `font.caption.size`,
127: `font.heading.1.size`–`font.heading.6.size` (with matching `.weight`/`.family`
128: paths), `font.mono.family`.
129: 
130: ### Spacing — Tier 1
131: 
132: Spacing is a **generative family** (Tailwind-v4 style): one base unit
133: multiplied by an arbitrary number.
134: 
135: | Token | Meaning |
136: |-------|---------|
137: | `space.base` | The spacing **unit** (F32) — override this to change the whole density |
138: | `space.<N>` | `space.base` × N, where N is any positive decimal (`space.1`, `space.2`, `space.0.5`, `space.3.75`) — **computed** by the resolver |
139: 
140: Rules:
141: 
142: 1. The `space.<N>` family is **generative**, not independently valued: the
143:    renderer resolves `space.base` and multiplies by the numeric leaf. Individual
144:    members MUST NOT be overridden via `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` — override `space.base`
145:    to control the whole scale.
146: 2. The color-scheme layer and parent fallback apply to `space.base`, never to an
147:    individual `space.<N>` member (`dark.space.2` is not a token; the dark layer
148:    is `dark.space.base`).
149: 3. A spacing/padding property MAY carry a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference to any
150:    `space.<N>` path — e.g. a DSL expresses `.padding(space.2)` or `Space(2)`.
151:    Literal F32 spacing values remain valid and unthemed.
152: 
153: Tier 2: `size.control.xs` / `sm` / `md` / `lg` — standard control heights.
154: 
155: ### Radius (roundings) — Tier 1
156: 
157: | Token | Meaning |
158: |-------|---------|
159: | `radius.xs` / `radius.sm` / `radius.md` / `radius.lg` / `radius.xl` | Corner radius scale (F32) |
160: | `radius.full` | Fully round (pill/circle) — renderer resolves to its "infinite" value |
161: 
162: ### Borders — Tier 1 core
163: 
164: | Token | Meaning |
165: |-------|---------|
166: | `border.width.thin` | Default hairline/border width |
167: 
168: Tier 2: `border.width.thick`.
169: 
170: ### Elevation — Tier 2
171: 
172: Shadows are composite; each component is its own token:
173: 
174: | Token | Meaning |
175: |-------|---------|
176: | `elevation.low.color` / `radius` / `x` / `y` / `blur` | Low elevation shadow |
177: | `elevation.high.color` / `radius` / `x` / `y` / `blur` | High elevation shadow |
178: 
179: ### Opacity — Tier 2
180: 
181: | Token | Meaning |
182: |-------|---------|
183: | `opacity.disabled` | The renderer MAY apply this to disabled controls. The disabled **state** itself is the `ENABLED` property; its visual handling (including this opacity) remains renderer-owned. |
184: 
185: ### Shared control core — Tier 1
186: 
187: Tokens every control-style component (buttons, inputs, switches, sliders, …)
188: shares. Renderers MUST resolve these; an individual token a renderer cannot
189: apply is ignored.
190: 
191: | Token | Meaning |
192: |-------|---------|
193: | `control.background` | Control resting background |
194: | `control.foreground` | Control content (label/icon) color |
195: | `control.border` | Control border color |
196: | `control.border.width` | Control border width |
197: | `control.radius` | Control corner radius |
198: | `control.padding.horizontal` / `control.padding.vertical` | Control inner padding |
199: | `control.height` | Control height (F32) |
200: | `control.font.size` / `control.font.weight` | Control text |
201: | `control.accent` | Control accent (fill, selection, focus) |
202: 
203: ### Per-component tokens
204: 
205: Small sets; only where a component's semantics genuinely differ from
206: `control.*`. All Tier 1 unless noted.
207: 
208: **Buttons** (Tier 1): `button.background`, `button.foreground`, `button.border`,
209: `button.radius`, `button.padding`, `button.height`, `button.font.size`,
210: `button.font.weight`, `button.accent`.
211: 
212: **Text fields / editors** (Tier 1): `input.background`, `input.foreground`,
213: `input.placeholder`, `input.border`, `input.radius`, `input.font.size`.
214: 
215: **Toggle / switch** (Tier 1): `toggle.accent`, `toggle.track.off`,
216: `toggle.track.on`, `toggle.thumb`.
217: 
218: **Slider** (Tier 1): `slider.accent`, `slider.track`, `slider.thumb`.
219: 
220: **Progress / gauge** (Tier 1): `progress.track`, `progress.fill`,
221: `gauge.track`, `gauge.fill`.
222: 
223: **Stepper** (Tier 2): `stepper.accent`, `stepper.background`, `stepper.border`,
224: `stepper.radius`.
225: 
226: **Picker** (Tier 2): `picker.accent`, `picker.background`, `picker.border`,
227: `picker.radius`.
228: 
229: **Menu** (Tier 2): `menu.background`, `menu.foreground`, `menu.border`,
230: `menu.radius`.
231: 
232: **Label** (Tier 2): `label.foreground`, `label.font.size`.
233: 
234: ---
235: 
236: ## Color Schemes (Light / Dark)
237: 
238: Base token paths define the **light** design. A `dark.`-prefixed path defines
239: the **dark** design for the same token.
240: 
241: The renderer derives the **effective color scheme** from the platform — it is
242: **never** carried by the protocol:
243: 
244: | Platform | Scheme signal |
245: |----------|---------------|
246: | Browser / HTML | `prefers-color-scheme` |
247: | GTK (desktop) | Native theme dark variant |
248: | Apple (SwiftUI/AppKit/UIKit) | `traitCollection` / `NSAppearance` / `@Environment(\.colorScheme)` |
249: | Android (Jetpack Compose) | `isSystemInDarkTheme()` |
250: | Windows (WinUI) | `Application.RequestedTheme` / `Element.ActualTheme` |
251: | Embedded (LVGL) | Renderer theme flag (no OS signal; base stays light unless enabled) |
252: 
253: ### Rules
254: 
255: 1. **Base = light.** `color.primary` is the light value; `dark.color.primary`
256:    is the dark value.
257: 2. A renderer MUST provide **both** light and dark defaults for every Tier 1
258:    token (platform-appropriate). Dark mode therefore works even when the
259:    application only overrides base tokens.
260: 3. The application rolls a full theme by overriding base values and — where the
261:    dark look must differ — `dark.*` values.
262: 4. The renderer MUST **re-resolve** every token-referencing property when the
263:    effective scheme changes, and MAY animate the transition.
264: 5. The `dark.` prefix is the first scheme prefix; the namespace is open so
265:    custom schemes could follow. Only `light` (base) and `dark` are
266:    standardized.
267: 
268: ---
269: 
270: ## Resolution
271: 
272: ```
273: FUNCTION resolveToken(tokenPath, scheme):
274:     # Walk most-specific → least-specific, applying the dark layer first.
275:     layers = []
276:     if scheme == dark:
277:         layers += [dark.path, dark.parent(path), …dark.root]   # dark.* layer
278:     layers += [path, parent(path), …root]                       # base layer
279: 
280:     for candidate in layers:
281:         if appOverrides.has(candidate):
282:             return appOverrides[candidate]
283:     for candidate in layers:
284:         if rendererDefaults.has(candidate):
285:             return rendererDefaults[candidate]
286:     return fallbackValue(path)
287: ```
288: 
289: Example — `color.primary` with the **dark** scheme active and only
290: `dark.color.primary` overridden:
291: 
292: 1. `dark.color.primary` — app override → **used**.
293: 2. (Unreached) `color.primary` app override, `dark.color.primary` renderer
294:    default, etc.
295: 
296: With the **light** scheme active:
297: 
298: 1. `color.primary` — app override, else renderer default, else parent/fallback.
299:    The `dark.*` layer is skipped entirely.
300: 
301: ### Generative token families
302: 
303: A **generative family** is a token rule rather than an independent value. Today
304: the `space` family is generative: `space.<N>` resolves by resolving `space.base`
305: (the scheme layer and parent fallback apply there) and multiplying by the
306: numeric leaf parsed from the path. This lets one override (`space.base`) drive
307: an arbitrarily fine spacing scale without per-step tokens. Only the `space`
308: family is generative today; other families could follow.
309: 
310: ---
311: 
312: ## References in properties
313: 
314: Any property whose value type is `COLOR` / `F32` / `STRING` / `ENUM` MAY instead
315: carry the **`DESIGN_TOKEN`** value type (`0x08`), with `C` = arenaRef to the
316: token path. The renderer resolves the reference against the token tables and the
317: current scheme, and re-resolves when the scheme changes.
318: 
319: - This is how a DSL expresses *semantic intent*: `.foregroundStyle(.primary)`
320:   or `Color.token("color.primary")` emits a token reference, not a packed color.
321: - A literal value and a token reference are mutually exclusive on a property.
322: - Because overrides and the scheme are renderer state, a token-typed property
323:   requires **no re-emission** when a token changes — the renderer re-resolves.
324: 
325: ---
326: 
327: ## Renderer Responsibilities
328: 
329: A renderer MUST:
330: 
331: 1. Provide platform-appropriate **light and dark defaults** for all Tier 1
332:    tokens.
333: 2. Accept `STYLE::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` commands and store overrides.
334: 3. Derive the effective color scheme from the platform and re-resolve on change.
335: 4. Resolve token references (`DESIGN_TOKEN` value type) in properties.
336: 5. Fall back to defaults when no override exists.
337: 6. Never transmit visual styling rules in the protocol.
338: 
339: A renderer MAY:
340: 
341: - Map tokens onto native semantic resources (system colors, platform
342:   typography) for its defaults.
343: - **Ignore** individual tokens it cannot apply (Tier 2, or Tier 1 tokens
344:   without a native equivalent) — the "allowed and ignored" rule modifiers use.
345: - Quantize / approximate token values to platform capabilities (e.g. RGB565
346:   color depth on embedded displays, limited font sets).
347: 
348: An application MAY override any token via `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` (base and `dark.*`)
349: and reference any token in a property; it MUST NOT assume specific default
350: values.
351: 
352: ---
353: 
354: ## Renderer Integration Contract
355: 
356: A future native renderer (SwiftUI/AppKit/UIKit, Jetpack Compose, WinUI, LVGL, …)
357: adopts the token system by implementing five pieces:
358: 
359: 1. **Default token table** — Tier 1 light + dark defaults from native resources.
360: 2. **Scheme detection** — the platform's native light/dark signal (table above).
361: 3. **Resolution** — the override → default → parent → fallback algorithm, with
362:    the `dark.*` layer keyed on the effective scheme.
363: 4. **Property resolution** — any property carrying a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference
364:    resolves to the concrete native value (e.g. a dynamic system color / theme
365:    resource / style value).
366: 5. **Re-resolution** — on scheme change, re-resolve and update the rendered
367:    output; animate if native.
368: 
369: The same contract powers the reference renderers (`pathland-render-html`,
370: `pathland-render-gtk`, the JS DOM renderer) and is checked in their `status.md`
371: files.
372: 
373: ### CSS variable mapping (HTML-family renderers)
374: 
375: HTML renderers map a token path to a CSS custom property deterministically so
376: server-side rendering and client hydration agree:
377: 
378: ```
379: tokenPathToVar("color.primary")      → --pl-color-primary
380: tokenPathToVar("dark.color.primary") → --pl-color-primary
381: ```
382: 
383: - The rule: `--pl-` prefix + the path with `.` → `-`. The `dark.` scheme prefix
384:   is **stripped** — the dark variant overrides the *same* variable, scoped
385:   inside the media query below.
386: - A **base** token is emitted as a plain `:root { --pl-…: value; }` rule.
387: - A `dark.*` token override is emitted **inside** `@media (prefers-color-scheme:
388:   dark) { :root { … } }` — never as a bare `--pl-dark-*` variable — so the
389:   browser resolves the scheme natively and server-side rendering needs no
390:   knowledge of the client's scheme.
391: - Inline `documentElement.style` overrides (the client delta path) MUST respect
392:   the same scoping; a dark override applied inline always would beat the media
393:   query and break light mode.

1: # pathland-render-html (Rust) — implementation status
2: 
3: **Last updated:** September 2, 2026
4: 
5: The **server-side / remote-projection HTML renderer**: a **stateless, streaming**
6: pure function of the opcode stream producing declarative HTML. Each render call
7: decodes a self-contained snapshot batch into a **transient** map, walks it once,
8: and emits HTML text out — no retained tree, zero cross-call state (Renderer
9: Statelessness). Protocol contract: `spec/`.
10: 
11: ## Implemented
12: 
13: - **Stateless streaming API**: `HtmlRenderer::render_document(opcodes, strings, root)`
14:   / `render_fragment(...)` build a transient decode map per call and stream HTML;
15:   the retained `apply`/`apply_frame`/`render` model is removed.
16: - **All spec components render**: `TEXT`, `IMAGE`, `COLOR` (layout-greedy:
17:   `flex:1;align-self:stretch`), `SHAPE` (CSS/SVG by `SHAPE_KIND`), `DIVIDER`, `SPACER`, `PROGRESS_VIEW`/`GAUGE`, `VSTACK`/
18:   `HSTACK`/`LAZY_VSTACK`/`LAZY_HSTACK` (flex), `ZSTACK` (overlay), `GRID`/
19:   `LAZY_VGRID`/`LAZY_HGRID` (CSS grid), `SCROLLVIEW`, `BUTTON`, `TEXT_FIELD`
20:   (incl. `IS_SECURE` → `type="password"`), `TEXT_EDITOR`, `TOGGLE`
21:   (`TOGGLE_STYLE`), `SLIDER`, `STEPPER`, `DATE_PICKER` (`SET_DATE` →
22:   `days_to_date`), `PICKER` (option children + `SELECTION`), `MENU`,
23:   `COLOR_PICKER`, `COMMENT`.
24: - **Composite override mode**: `BUTTON`/`TOGGLE`/`SLIDER` with children render
25:   the custom body wrapped in the native element.
26: - **Properties**: `ALIGNMENT` (cross-axis flex), `CONTENT_MARGINS`,
27:   `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` (`FILL`/`HUG`), `PADDING` + per-edge, `COLOR`,
28:   `BACKGROUND_COLOR`, `FONT_SIZE`/`WEIGHT`/`FAMILY`, `OPACITY`, `VISIBLE`,
29:   `Z_INDEX`, `LINE_LIMIT`, `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`, `TRUNCATION_MODE`, `BORDER_*`,
30:   `SELECTED`, `TOGGLE_STYLE`, `ENABLED`, `ROLE`/`STATE` (ARIA), plus
31:   `TEXT_CASE`, `FONT_STYLE`, `FONT_DESIGN`, `UNDERLINE`/`STRIKETHROUGH`,
32:   `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`, `ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING`, `COLOR_INVERT`.
33: - **Event surfacing**: `data-event-listeners` / `data-action-id` /
34:   `data-binding-id` attributes.
35: - `STYLE::SET_DATE` handled (days + millis-of-day → date/time).
36: - **Design tokens (spec/TOKENS.md)**:
37:   - `STYLE::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides are collected per snapshot batch and
38:     emitted into the document head as CSS: base (light) tokens as `:root`
39:     rules, `dark.*` overrides inside `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` —
40:     the browser resolves the scheme natively, so SSR needs no client scheme.
41:   - `DESIGN_TOKEN`-typed `SET_PROPERTY` values resolve at render time to
42:     `var(--pl-…)`, with the generative `space.<N>` family resolving to
43:     `calc(var(--pl-space-base) * N)` (`Node::token_ref`).
44:   - The built-in `:root` tokens use the **canonical spec paths** (`--pl-color-primary`,
45:     `--pl-color-background`, `--pl-color-text-primary`, `--pl-color-text-secondary`,
46:     `--pl-color-surface`, `--pl-color-border`) so app overrides retheme the
47:     renderer.
48: 
49: ## Design decision (decision A, September 2026): inline-all + built-in design system
50: 
51: Tailwind is **removed**. The renderer emits **everything inline** as CSS in a
52: single `style` attribute — no external compiler, no class system, no safelist:
53: 
54: - **All opcode properties render inline** (`style_css()` + `border_style()`),
55:   including the previously class-based enum surface (alignment, text alignment,
56:   text case, visible, font style/design, underline/strikethrough, clips-to-bounds,
57:   hit-testing, invert, truncation). **1 dp = 1 CSS px**.
58: - **`css::STYLE`** is a built-in `<style>` block injected by `render_document`,
59:   containing:
60:   - a **preflight reset** (vendored from Tailwind CSS, MIT — see
61:     `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES`),
62:   - `:root` **design tokens** as CSS custom properties (`--pl-color-primary`,
63:     `--pl-color-background` (document background), `--pl-color-surface`,
64:     `--pl-color-text-primary`/`--pl-color-text-secondary`, `--pl-color-border`,
65:     `--pl-radius-*`, `--pl-font-sans`, `--pl-input-*` (field bg/text/outline/
66:     placeholder/focus), button tokens), named to match the canonical protocol
67:     design-token paths so `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` can retheme the renderer,
68:   - `.pathland-button` (the prettified-button POC, with `prefers-color-scheme`
69:     dark mode) and `.pathland-*` component defaults (toggle switch, slider, text
70:     field/editor, stepper, spinner, gauge, menu) — the interactive/hover/focus/
71:     disabled states that can't be expressed inline. Text fields use a
72:     Tailwind-style **inset outline** (`outline: 1px solid`, `outline-offset: -1px`,
73:     focus → `2px`/`-2px` + indigo) instead of a border, with dark-mode tokens;
74:     `html` sets `color-scheme: light dark` + the `--pl-color-bg` background so
75:     native form controls and the page follow the theme.
76: - **`pathland_html_*` cdylib** (`pathland_html_render` / `_render_fragment` /
77:   `_free`) for cross-language hosts (Java JNA shim). The `_tailwind_compile`
78:   entry point, `tw.rs`, `tailwind.rs`, `build.rs`, `scripts/fetch-tailwind.mjs`,
79:   `vendor/`, and the `tailwind-embed` feature are **deleted**.
80: 
81: ## Not implemented / gaps
82: 
83: - **`DESIGN_TOKEN` property references** cover the directly-mappable subset
84:   (colors, font size/weight, spacing/padding, corner radius, opacity,
85:   width/height, border width/color, shadow color). Compound accumulators that
86:   need concrete numbers (shadow radius/x/y) remain literal-only.
87: - **`STRING`-valued token overrides** (e.g. `font.body.family`) are not yet
88:   supported on the wire path (deferred).
89: - The built-in `:root` **component-level tokens** (`--pl-input-*`, `--pl-button-*`,
90:   `--pl-shadow-sm`, `--pl-color-focus-ring`) are still renderer-internal; mapping
91:   them onto the canonical `control.*`/`button.*`/`input.*` catalog is a follow-up.
92: - `SHAPE` `Path` renders as an SVG placeholder (no path data wire property).
93: - GAUGE/SHAPE visuals are CSS approximations, not pixel-exact.
94: - **Inter is loaded from the rsms.me CDN** (Cloudflare, `font-display: swap`,
95:   with the InterVariable progressive enhancement for variable-font browsers) —
96:   the renderer emits the preconnect + stylesheet links in the document head. It
97:   is **not bundled**: self-hosting a subsetted, OFL-licensed woff2 (embedded in
98:   the renderer / jar) is a planned follow-up for offline and enterprise
99:   deployments (see `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES`).
100: 
101: ## Verified by
102: 
103: `cargo test -p pathland-render-html` — 32 headless render tests (components,
104: properties, composite, event attrs, `days_to_date`, network-decoded frames,
105: inline-all styling, built-in CSS block contents, Inter CDN head links, design
106: tokens: base/dark override CSS, `px` lengths, `DESIGN_TOKEN` refs,
107: generative `space.N`).

(End of file - total 107 lines)
</content>

## The main gap: GTK renderer has no design-token support

The design-token work landed everywhere **except** `pathland-render-gtk` (recent commits: `61b02ec` spec, `f0e776e` HTML/JS DOM renderers, `bacf1e4` Rust DSL/engine, `980e345` Java DSL). GTK is now the only renderer that ignores tokens:

- `host.rs:147` — `STYLE::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` is **swallowed** (`let _ = op;`)
- `host.rs:128-141` — `SET_PROPERTY` treats a `DESIGN_TOKEN`-typed value as a raw `u32` (stores the arena offset, never resolves the path), while `STRING` is handled
- No default token table (Tier 1 light+dark), no scheme detection, no re-resolution

This violates the `spec/TOKENS.md` renderer contract (a renderer MUST: provide light+dark Tier 1 defaults, accept `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`, derive the effective scheme, resolve `DESIGN_TOKEN` refs, fall back to defaults). Note GTK CSS has no `var()`/custom properties, so resolution must happen in Rust at apply time (vs. the HTML renderers' `var(--pl-…)`).

## Related (already documented) outstanding items

- Rust DSL `pathland-view/status.md:35` — no `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` global override helper / `Theme` object
- Java `pathland-view/status.md:110` — same, no `setDesignToken` on the emitter/sink
- `pathland-render-gtk/status.md` — doesn't mention design tokens at all (out of sync)

1. New `tokens.rs` (or module in `host.rs`): a `Theme` with built-in Tier 1 light/dark defaults + app overrides (`HashMap<String, (u8, u32)>`), the `dark.*` layer, and the `space.<N>` generative family (`space.base` × N).
2. `host.rs`: parse `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` (arena path, valueType, value) into the store; resolve `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type in `SET_PROPERTY` to a concrete value at apply time, recording that it's token-backed.
3. Scheme detection via `gtk::Settings` (`gtk-application-prefer-dark-theme`/theme-name) + `notify` handler to re-apply token-backed properties (re-run the existing CSS-provider/Pango paths).
4. Wire token resolution into the existing apply paths: colors → `style_css()`/Pango color, font size/weight → Pango, spacing/padding → margins/spacing, radius → `border-radius`, etc. (mirroring HTML's `token_ref` resolution).
5. Update `pathland-render-gtk/status.md`.

Branch: `feature/design-tokens-theming` (6 commits, clean tree). It implements
the **design-token system / theming** end-to-end. The canonical contract is
`spec/TOKENS.md`:

- Tokens are dot-separated paths (`color.primary`, `space.2`). **base = light**;
  `dark.`-prefixed paths are the dark variant (`dark.color.primary`).
- **Scheme selection is renderer-derived** (browser `prefers-color-scheme`,
  GTK native variant). There is deliberately NO `META::SET_THEME` — do not add one.
- Any `COLOR`/`F32`/`STRING`/`ENUM` property MAY carry the **`DESIGN_TOKEN`**

- `STYLE::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` (A=arenaRef path, B=valueType, C=value) is a global

  scheme.
- Spacing is a **generative family**: `space.<N>` resolves to `space.base × N`.

- CSS variable mapping: `--pl-` + path with `.` → `-` (the `dark.` prefix is
  stripped — the dark variant overrides the same variable inside the media query).

308: A color property carrying a **token reference** instead of a literal: the
309: renderer resolves `"color.primary"` (arena entry at offset 0) against the token
310: tables and the current scheme.
311: 
312: ```
313: 02 01 00 00 01 00 00 00 0A 10 08 00 00 00 00 00
314: ```
315: 
316: - `02` category = STYLE
317: - `01` command = SET_PROPERTY
318: - `00 00` flags = 0
319: - `01 00 00 00` A = nodeId = 1
320: - `0A 10 08 00` B = `(valueType << 16) | propertyId` = `(0x08 << 16) | 0x100A`
321:   - low two bytes `0A 10` = propertyId = 0x100A (COLOR)
322:   - high byte `08` = valueType = 0x08 (DESIGN_TOKEN)
323: - `00 00 00 00` C = arenaRef = 0 (`"color.primary"`)
324: 
325: ### 19. NETWORK:BATCH (frameCount=3, one DESIGN_TOKEN-referencing SET_PROPERTY, arena delta = "color.primary")
326: 
327: The single opcode is vector 18. The arena delta is the self-describing entry for
328: `"color.primary"`: `[0D 00 00 00][63 6F 6C 6F 72 2E 70 72 69 6D 61 72 79]`.
329: 
330: ```
331: 4C 50 4C 50 01 00 00 00 03 00 00 00 01 00 00 00
332: 02 01 00 00 01 00 00 00 0A 10 08 00 00 00 00 00
333: 11 00 00 00 0D 00 00 00 63 6F 6C 6F 72 2E 70 72 69 6D 61 72 79
334: ```
335: 
336: - `4C 50 4C 50` = magic `PLPL` (u32 `0x504C504C`, little-endian)
337: - `01 00` = version 1
338: - `00 00` = flags (guest → host)
339: - `03 00 00 00` = frameCount = 3
340: - `01 00 00 00` = opcodeCount = 1
341: - `02 01 00 00 01 00 00 00 0A 10 08 00 00 00 00 00` = the SET_PROPERTY opcode (16 bytes)
342: - `11 00 00 00` = arenaDeltaLen = 17
343: - `0D 00 00 00 63 6F 6C 6F 72 2E 70 72 69 6D 61 72 79` = arena entry `[len=13]["color.primary"]`
344: 
345: ---
346: 
347: ## Design-Token Resolution Conformance
348: 
349: The token system (catalog, override/default resolution, `dark.` color-scheme
350: layer) is defined in [TOKENS.md](./TOKENS.md). Resolution is a renderer behavior
351: and is not byte-encodable; a conforming renderer MUST produce these outcomes.
352: 
353: Given the overrides:
354: 
355: | Token override (via `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`) | Value |
356: |------------------------------------------|-------|
357: | `color.primary` | `0xFF2563EB` |
358: | `dark.color.primary` | `0xFF60A5FA` |
359: | `space.base` | `4.0` (F32) |
360: 
361: | Query | Active scheme | Resolves to | Rationale |
362: |-------|---------------|-------------|-----------|
363: | `color.primary` | dark | `0xFF60A5FA` | `dark.color.primary` override wins (dark layer) |
364: | `color.primary` | light | `0xFF2563EB` | dark layer skipped; base override wins |
365: | `color.primary` | dark, no `dark.*` override | base override `0xFF2563EB` | base override falls through when the dark layer is empty |
366: | `font.body.size` | either | renderer default | no override; defaults are renderer-owned |
367: | `font.body.size` | either, override only `font.body` | the `font.body` override | parent-path fallback |
368: | `space.2` | either | `8.0` | generative family: `space.base` (4.0) × 2 |
369: | `space.0.5` | either | `2.0` | generative family: fractional leaf |
370: | `space.2` | either, `space.base` not overridden | renderer default × 2 | generative base falls back to renderer defaults |
371: 
372: A property carrying the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type (vector 18) resolves through
373: the same algorithm and MUST re-resolve when the active scheme changes.

528: /// Decode a self-contained snapshot batch (opcodes + string section) into a
529: /// **transient** `id → Node` map. The map lives only for the duration of one
530: /// render call — the renderer retains nothing between calls.
531: fn decode(opcodes: &[Opcode], strings: &[u8]) -> (BTreeMap<u32, Node>, Tokens) {
532:     let mut nodes = BTreeMap::new();
533:     let mut tokens = Tokens::default();
534:     for op in opcodes {
535:         match op.category() {
536:             category::TREE => apply_tree(&mut nodes, op.command(), *op),
537:             category::STYLE => {
538:                 if op.command() == style::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN {
539:                     // Global override: A = arenaRef (token path), B = valueType, C = value.
540:                     if let Some(path) = strings_str(strings, op.a()) {
541:                         tokens.set(&path, (op.b() & 0xFF) as u8, op.c());
542:                     }
543:                 } else {
544:                     apply_style(&mut nodes, op.command(), *op, strings);
545:                 }
546:             }
547:             _ => {}
548:         }
549:     }
550:     (nodes, tokens)
551: }
552: 
553: /// Read a `[u32 len][utf8]` entry from the batch's string section at a relative offset.
554: fn strings_str(strings: &[u8], offset: u32) -> Option<String> {
555:     let offset = offset as usize;
556:     if offset + 4 > strings.len() {
557:         return None;
558:     }
559:     let len = u32::from_le_bytes(strings[offset..offset + 4].try_into().ok()?) as usize;
560:     let start = offset + 4;
561:     if start + len > strings.len() {
562:         return None;
563:     }
564:     std::str::from_utf8(&strings[start..start + len]).ok().map(str::to_owned)
565: }

567: // --- Design tokens (spec/TOKENS.md) ---
568: 
569: /// `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides collected from a snapshot batch. `base` holds
570: /// light tokens (keyed by full path); `dark` holds `dark.`-prefixed overrides
571: /// (keyed by the bare path).
572: #[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]
573: struct Tokens {
574:     base: BTreeMap<String, (u8, u32)>,
575:     dark: BTreeMap<String, (u8, u32)>,
576: }
577: 
578: impl Tokens {
579:     fn set(&mut self, path: &str, value_type: u8, value: u32) {
580:         if let Some(bare) = path.strip_prefix("dark.") {
581:             self.dark.insert(bare.to_string(), (value_type, value));
582:         } else {
583:             self.base.insert(path.to_string(), (value_type, value));
584:         }
585:     }
586: 
587:     /// Render the overrides as CSS rules: base tokens as `:root` rules, dark
588:     /// overrides inside `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` — the browser
589:     /// resolves the scheme natively, so SSR needs no client scheme knowledge.
590:     fn css(&self) -> String {
591:         let mut css = String::new();
592:         for (path, (vt, value)) in &self.base {
593:             css.push_str(&format!(
594:                 ":root{{{}:{};}}",
595:                 token_to_css_var(path),
596:                 token_css_value(path, *vt, *value)
597:             ));
598:         }
599:         if !self.dark.is_empty() {
600:             let rules: String = self
601:                 .dark
602:                 .iter()
603:                 .map(|(path, (vt, value))| {
604:                     format!(":root{{{}:{};}}", token_to_css_var(path), token_css_value(path, *vt, *value))
605:                 })
606:                 .collect();
607:             css.push_str(&format!("@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark){{{rules}}}"));
608:         }
609:         css
610:     }
611: }

613: /// The canonical CSS custom property for a token path: `--pl-` prefix, `.` →
614: /// `-`. The `dark.` scheme prefix is stripped — the dark variant overrides the
615: /// same variable inside the media query (spec/TOKENS.md).
616: fn token_to_css_var(path: &str) -> String {
617:     let name: String = path
618:         .chars()
619:         .map(|c| if c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '-' || c == '_' { c } else { '-' })
620:         .collect();
621:     format!("--pl-{name}")
622: }

624: /// Token paths whose F32 values are CSS lengths (emitted with `px`).
625: fn is_length_token(path: &str) -> bool {
626:     if path.starts_with("space.")
627:         || path.starts_with("radius.")
628:         || path.starts_with("border.width.")
629:         || path.starts_with("size.control.")
630:         || path.starts_with("control.padding.")
631:         || path.starts_with("control.height.")

641:     if path.starts_with("font.heading.") && path.ends_with(".size") {

643:     }
644:     path.starts_with("elevation.")

646: }

650: fn token_css_value(path: &str, value_type: u8, value: u32) -> String {
651:     match value_type {
652:         value_type::COLOR => rgba(value),
653:         value_type::F32 => {
654:             let v = f32::from_bits(value);
655:             if is_length_token(path) {

657:             } else {
658:                 format!("{v}")

660:         }
661:         value_type::I32 => format!("{}", value as i32),
662:         value_type::U32 => format!("{}", value),
663:         value_type::U8 => format!("{}", value & 0xFF),
664:         _ => format!("{}", value),
665:     }
666: }

675:             return format!("calc(var(--pl-space-base) * {rest})");
676:         }
677:     }

9: import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
10: import java.util.ArrayList;
11: import java.util.List;
12: 
13: /**
14:  * An {@link OpcodeSink} that accumulates a self-contained {@link Frame} (opcodes +
15:  * string section) entirely in the JVM. This is the SSR / WebSocket path: the frame is
16:  * rendered to HTML or encoded to the network batch wire format.
17:  */
18: public class FrameOpcodeSink implements OpcodeSink {
19: 
20:     private final List<Opcode> opcodes = new ArrayList<>();
21:     private final ByteArrayOutputStream strings = new ByteArrayOutputStream();
22:     private Frame frame = Frame.EMPTY;
23:     private int framesProduced;
24: 
25:     /** The frame built by the last {@code beginFrame/endFrame} pair. */
26:     public Frame frame() {
27:         return frame;
28:     }
29: 
30:     /** Number of completed frames so far (unchanged signals do not produce a frame). */
31:     public int framesProduced() {
32:         return framesProduced;
33:     }
34: 
35:     public boolean hasChanges() {
36:         return !opcodes.isEmpty();
37:     }
38: 
39:     @Override
40:     public void beginFrame() {
41:         opcodes.clear();
42:         strings.reset();
43:     }
44: 
45:     @Override
46:     public void endFrame() {
47:         frame = new Frame(List.copyOf(opcodes), strings.toByteArray());
48:         framesProduced++;
49:     }
50: 
51:     @Override
52:     public void createNode(int id, int component) {
53:         push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.CREATE_NODE, 0, id, component, 0);
54:     }
55: 
56:     @Override
57:     public void deleteNode(int id) {
58:         push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.DELETE_NODE, 0, id, 0, 0);
59:     }
60: 
61:     @Override
62:     public void insertChild(int parent, int child, int index) {
63:         push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.INSERT_CHILD, 0, parent, child, index);
64:     }
65: 
66:     @Override
67:     public void removeChild(int parent, int child) {
68:         push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.REMOVE_CHILD, 0, parent, child, 0);
69:     }
70: 
71:     @Override
72:     public void moveChild(int parent, int child, int newIndex) {
73:         push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.MOVE_CHILD, 0, parent, child, newIndex);
74:     }
75: 
76:     @Override
77:     public void setText(int nodeId, String text) {
78:         int offset = strings.size();
79:         writeString(text);
80:         push(Categories.STYLE, Commands.Style.SET_TEXT, 0, nodeId, offset, 0);
81:     }
82: 
83:     @Override
84:     public void setProperty(int nodeId, int property, int valueType, Object value) {
85:         int b = (valueType << 16) | (property & 0xFFFF);
86:         if (valueType == ValueTypes.STRING) {
87:             int offset = strings.size();
88:             writeString((String) value);
89:             push(Categories.STYLE, Commands.Style.SET_PROPERTY, 0, nodeId, b, offset);
90:         } else if (valueType == ValueTypes.DESIGN_TOKEN) {
91:             // C = arena offset of the token path (spec/TOKENS.md).
92:             int offset = strings.size();
93:             writeString(((Color) value).token());
94:             push(Categories.STYLE, Commands.Style.SET_PROPERTY, 0, nodeId, b, offset);
95:         } else {
96:             push(Categories.STYLE, Commands.Style.SET_PROPERTY, 0, nodeId, b, ValueEncoder.encodeBits(valueType, value));
97:         }
98:     }
99: 
100:     @Override
101:     public void setDate(int nodeId, int days, int millisOfDay) {
102:         push(Categories.STYLE, Commands.Style.SET_DATE, 0, nodeId, days, millisOfDay);
103:     }
104: 
105:     /** Append a length-prefixed string to the string section, returning its offset. */
106:     public int writeString(String text) {
107:         int offset = strings.size();
108:         byte[] utf8 = text.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
109:         writeIntLE(utf8.length);
110:         strings.writeBytes(utf8);
111:         return offset;
112:     }
113: 
114:     private void push(int category, int command, int flags, int a, int b, int c) {
115:         opcodes.add(new Opcode(category, command, flags, a, b, c));
116:     }
117: 
118:     private void writeIntLE(int value) {
119:         strings.write(value & 0xFF);
120:         strings.write((value >>> 8) & 0xFF);
121:         strings.write((value >>> 16) & 0xFF);
122:         strings.write((value >>> 24) & 0xFF);
123:     }
124: }

1: //! Golden conformance vectors for the network batch format.
2: //!
3: //! These byte arrays are the canonical wire representation (see
4: //! `spec/CONFORMANCE.md`). A conforming implementation MUST encode and decode
5: //! these exactly.
6: 
7: #[cfg(test)]
8: mod tests {
9:     use crate::batch::{encode_batch, BatchDecoder};
10:     use pathland_core::{category, Opcode};
11: 
12:     /// The canonical bytes for `NETWORK:BATCH` vector 13 (see CONFORMANCE.md).
13:     const VECTOR_13: &[u8] = &[
14:         0x4C, 0x50, 0x4C, 0x50, // magic PLPL (LE)
15:         0x01, 0x00, // version 1
16:         0x00, 0x00, // flags guest->host
17:         0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, // frameCount = 1
18:         0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, // opcodeCount = 1
19:         0x01, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x10, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
20:         0x00, // CREATE_NODE (id=1, VSTACK)
21:         0x06, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, // arenaDeltaLen = 6
22:         0x02, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x48, 0x69, // arena entry [len=2]["Hi"]
23:     ];
24: 
25:     /// The canonical bytes for `NETWORK:BATCH` vector 14 (see CONFORMANCE.md).
26:     const VECTOR_14: &[u8] = &[
27:         0x4C, 0x50, 0x4C, 0x50, // magic PLPL (LE)
28:         0x01, 0x00, // version 1
29:         0x00, 0x00, // flags
30:         0x02, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, // frameCount = 2
31:         0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, // opcodeCount = 0
32:         0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, // arenaDeltaLen = 0
33:     ];
34: 
35:     #[test]
36:     fn vector_13_encode_exactly() {
37:         let opcodes = [Opcode::new(category::TREE, 0x01, 0, 1, 0x0010, 0)];
38:         let arena_delta = [0x02, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x48, 0x69];
39:         let bytes = encode_batch(1, 0, &opcodes, &arena_delta);
40:         assert_eq!(bytes, VECTOR_13);
41:     }
42: 
43:     #[test]
44:     fn vector_14_encode_exactly() {
45:         let bytes = encode_batch(2, 0, &[], &[]);
46:         assert_eq!(bytes, VECTOR_14);
47:     }
48: 
49:     #[test]
50:     fn vectors_decode_and_round_trip() {
51:         for bytes in [VECTOR_13, VECTOR_14] {
52:             let mut decoder = BatchDecoder::new();
53:             let batch = decoder.decode(bytes).unwrap();
54:             assert_eq!(batch.flags(), 0);
55:             let reencoded = {
56:                 let opcodes: Vec<Opcode> = batch.opcodes().collect();
57:                 // The decoder has already mirrored the arena delta; re-encoding
58:                 // with an empty delta produces a valid follow-up batch.
59:                 encode_batch(batch.frame_count(), batch.flags(), &opcodes, &[])
60:             };
61:             // Decoding again (empty delta appended to mirror) must stay valid.
62:             let _ = decoder.decode(&reencoded).unwrap();
63:         }
64:     }
65: }

14: /**
15:  * An {@link OpcodeSink} that writes opcodes zero-copy into the Rust SPSC ring via
16:  * JNA. Strings are allocated into the shared bump arena (absolute offsets). This is the
17:  * desktop/embedded path; the frame path uses {@code FrameOpcodeSink} instead.
18:  */
19: public final class RingOpcodeSink implements OpcodeSink, AutoCloseable {
20: 
21:     private final PathlandCore core;
22:     private final Pointer handle;
23: 
24:     public RingOpcodeSink() {
25:         this(PathlandCore.instance());
26:     }
27: 
28:     public RingOpcodeSink(PathlandCore core) {
29:         this.core = core;
30:         this.handle = core.create();
31:     }
32: 
33:     /** The opaque native handle (for direct ring access). */
34:     public Pointer handle() {
35:         return handle;
36:     }
37: 
38:     @Override
39:     public void beginFrame() {
40:         core.beginFrame(handle);
41:     }
42: 
43:     @Override
44:     public void endFrame() {
45:         core.endFrame(handle);
46:     }
47: 
48:     @Override
49:     public void createNode(int id, int component) {
50:         push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.CREATE_NODE, 0, id, component, 0);
51:     }
52: 
53:     @Override
54:     public void deleteNode(int id) {
55:         push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.DELETE_NODE, 0, id, 0, 0);
56:     }
57: 
58:     @Override
59:     public void insertChild(int parent, int child, int index) {
60:         push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.INSERT_CHILD, 0, parent, child, index);
61:     }
62: 
63:     @Override
64:     public void removeChild(int parent, int child) {
65:         push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.REMOVE_CHILD, 0, parent, child, 0);
66:     }
67: 
68:     @Override
69:     public void moveChild(int parent, int child, int newIndex) {
70:         push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.MOVE_CHILD, 0, parent, child, newIndex);
71:     }
72: 
73:     @Override
74:     public void setText(int nodeId, String text) {
75:         int ref = core.arenaAlloc(handle, text.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
76:         push(Categories.STYLE, Commands.Style.SET_TEXT, 0, nodeId, ref, 0);
77:     }
78: 
79:     @Override
80:     public void setProperty(int nodeId, int property, int valueType, Object value) {
81:         int b = (valueType << 16) | (property & 0xFFFF);
82:         if (valueType == ValueTypes.STRING) {
83:             int ref = core.arenaAlloc(handle, ((String) value).getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
84:             push(Categories.STYLE, Commands.Style.SET_PROPERTY, 0, nodeId, b, ref);
85:         } else if (valueType == ValueTypes.DESIGN_TOKEN) {
86:             int ref = core.arenaAlloc(handle, ((Color) value).token().getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
87:             push(Categories.STYLE, Commands.Style.SET_PROPERTY, 0, nodeId, b, ref);
88:         } else {
89:             push(Categories.STYLE, Commands.Style.SET_PROPERTY, 0, nodeId, b,
90:                     ValueEncoder.encodeBits(valueType, value));
91:         }
92:     }
93: 
94:     @Override
95:     public void setDate(int nodeId, int days, int millisOfDay) {
96:         push(Categories.STYLE, Commands.Style.SET_DATE, 0, nodeId, days, millisOfDay);
97:     }
98: 
99:     private void push(int category, int command, int flags, int a, int b, int c) {
100:         core.push(handle, new Opcode(category, command, flags, a, b, c).toBytes());
101:     }
102: 
103:     @Override
104:     public void close() {
105:         core.destroy(handle);
106:     }
107: }

2: // properties (spec/TOKENS.md). Base (light) tokens are emitted as `:root`
3: // rules; `dark.*` overrides are emitted inside
4: // `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` so the browser resolves the scheme
5: // natively. A managed <style> element is used instead of inline
6: // `documentElement.style` — an inline dark override would beat the media query
7: // and break light mode.
8: 
9: import type { Batch, Opcode } from "./plpl";
10: import { readString } from "./plpl";
11: import { VAL_COLOR, VAL_F32, VAL_I32, VAL_U8, VAL_U32 } from "./constants";
12: import { argbToRgba, f32FromBits } from "./format";
13: 
14: const DARK_PREFIX = "dark.";
15: 
16: /** The canonical CSS custom property for a token path (spec/TOKENS.md): `--pl-`
17:  *  prefix, `.` → `-`. The `dark.` scheme prefix is stripped — the dark variant
18:  *  overrides the same variable inside a media query. */
19: export function tokenToCssVar(path: string): string {
20:   const bare = path.startsWith(DARK_PREFIX) ? path.slice(DARK_PREFIX.length) : path;
21:   return "--pl-" + bare.replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/g, "-");
22: }
23: 
24: /** Whether a token path selects the dark variant. */
25: export function isDarkToken(path: string): boolean {
26:   return path.startsWith(DARK_PREFIX);
27: }
28: 
29: /** Token paths whose F32 values are CSS lengths (emitted with `px`). */
30: function isLengthToken(path: string): boolean {
31:   if (
32:     path.startsWith("space.") ||
33:     path.startsWith("radius.") ||
34:     path.startsWith("border.width.") ||
35:     path.startsWith("size.control.") ||
36:     path.startsWith("control.padding.") ||
37:     path.startsWith("control.height.")
38:   ) {
39:     return true;
40:   }
41:   if (path.startsWith("control.font.") && path.endsWith(".size")) {
42:     return true;
43:   }
44:   if (path === "font.body.size" || path === "font.caption.size") {
45:     return true;
46:   }
47:   if (/^font\.heading\.\d+\.size$/.test(path)) {
48:     return true;
49:   }
50:   return /^elevation\.(low|high)\.(radius|x|y|blur)$/.test(path);
51: }
52: 
53: /** Render a token value as a CSS value string per the value type. */
54: export function tokenCssValue(valueType: number, c: number): string {
55:   switch (valueType) {
56:     case VAL_COLOR:
57:       return argbToRgba(c);
58:     case VAL_F32:
59:       return String(f32FromBits(c));
60:     case VAL_I32:
61:       return String(c | 0);
62:     case VAL_U32:
63:       return String(c >>> 0);
64:     case VAL_U8:
65:       return String(c & 0xff);
66:     default:
67:       return String(c >>> 0);
68:   }
69: }
70: 
71: /** Render a token override value as CSS, appending `px` to F32 length tokens. */
72: function tokenCssOverride(path: string, valueType: number, c: number): string {
73:   const value = tokenCssValue(valueType, c);
74:   return isLengthToken(path) && valueType === VAL_F32 ? value + "px" : value;
75: }
76: 
77: const SPACE_FAMILY = /^space\.(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)$/;
78: 
79: /** Resolve a token *reference* (in a property) to a CSS expression. The
80:  *  generative `space.<N>` family resolves to `calc(var(--pl-space-base) * N)`;
81:  *  every other token resolves to `var(--pl-<path>)`. */
82: export function resolveTokenCssRef(path: string): string {
83:   const m = SPACE_FAMILY.exec(path);
84:   if (m) {
85:     return `calc(var(--pl-space-base) * ${m[1]})`;
86:   }
87:   return `var(${tokenToCssVar(path)})`;
88: }
89: 
90: export interface DesignTokenSink {
91:   setToken(path: string, valueType: number, c: number): void;
92: }
93: 
94: /**
95:  * Applies token overrides to a managed `<style data-pathland-tokens>` element:
96:  * base tokens as `:root` rules, `dark.*` tokens inside
97:  * `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)`. The element is appended to `<head>`
98:  * after the SSR built-in style block, so equal-specificity rules win in order.
99:  */
100: export function createTokenSink(): DesignTokenSink {
101:   const base = new Map<string, string>();
102:   const dark = new Map<string, string>();
103:   let styleEl: HTMLStyleElement | null = null;
104: 
105:   function render(): void {
106:     const rules: string[] = [];
107:     for (const [name, value] of base) {
108:       rules.push(`:root{${name}:${value};}`);
109:     }
110:     if (dark.size > 0) {
111:       const darkRules: string[] = [];
112:       for (const [name, value] of dark) {
113:         darkRules.push(`:root{${name}:${value};}`);
114:       }
115:       rules.push(`@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark){${darkRules.join("")}}`);
116:     }
117:     if (!styleEl) {
118:       styleEl = document.createElement("style");
119:       styleEl.setAttribute("data-pathland-tokens", "");
120:       document.head.appendChild(styleEl);

122:     styleEl.textContent = rules.join("");
123:   }
124: 
125:   return {
126:     setToken(path, valueType, c) {
127:       const name = tokenToCssVar(path);
128:       const value = tokenCssOverride(path, valueType, c);
129:       (isDarkToken(path) ? dark : base).set(name, value);
130:       render();
131:     },
132:   };
133: }

140:   const path = readString(strings, op.a);

1: //! # Pathland GTK4 desktop demo
2: //!
3: //! A native GTK4 app demonstrating Pathland's **zero-copy shared-memory ring**
4: //! and the shared **GTK renderer** (`pathland-render-gtk`).
5: //!
6: //! The developer authors the UI with the SwiftUI-style DSL; the diff emitter in
7: //! `pathland-core` emits declarative 16-byte opcodes into the shared ring, and
8: //! the `pathland-render-gtk` renderer maps them onto native GTK widgets. The demo
9: //! never touches GTK/glib/pango directly — it only drives Pathland and the
10: //! renderer.
11: //!
12: //! Interaction is declared with `.on_tap_gesture(...)` on any view; raw pointer
13: //! events round-trip through the shared ring and are turned back into taps by
14: //! the app-side [`TapRecognizer`](pathland_view::TapRecognizer).
15: 
16: use std::cell::RefCell;
17: use std::collections::BTreeMap;
18: use std::rc::Rc;
19: use std::time::Instant;
20: 
21: use pathland_engine::Engine;
22: use pathland_core::{listener, size};
23: use pathland_core_transport::RingTransport;
24: use pathland_view::{assign_ids, button, hstack, text, vstack, Align, Color, Node, View, ViewExt};
25: 
26: const APP_ID: &str = "org.pathland.GtkDemo";
27: 
28: /// node id → tap callback, collected from the built tree after `assign_ids`.
29: type TapHandlers = BTreeMap<u32, Rc<RefCell<dyn FnMut() + 'static>>>;
30: 
31: /// Build the DSL tree for the current counter value. This is the developer's
32: /// authoring surface.
33: fn build_tree(count: &Rc<RefCell<u32>>) -> Node {
34:     let tap_count = count.clone();
35:     vstack![
36:         hstack![
37:             text(format!("Count: {}", *count.borrow()).as_str())

40: /// The bidirectional transport surface the renderer pumps: frames in
41: /// (guest → host) and events out (host → guest).
42: ///
43: /// The renderer **never drains events** — it only writes them as `EVENT`
44: /// opcodes. The host (application) drains the event ring itself, so raw inputs
45: /// return to the app through the opcode engine, symmetric with how frames flow

48:     /// Read the next guest → host frame.
49:     fn next_frame(&mut self) -> Result<Option<OpcodeBatch<'_>>, TransportError>;

500: - The **application** declares a theme: token overrides (base = **light**
501:   design, `dark.`-prefixed = **dark** design) and token references in style
502:   properties.
503: - The **renderer** supplies platform-appropriate defaults, derives the
504:   effective color scheme from the platform, resolves token references, and
505:   owns hover/pressed/focus/disabled styling.
506: 
507: This ensures a native look-and-feel by default and cross-platform consistency
508: when the application rolls a theme.
509: 
510: ### Tokens & color schemes
511: 
512: - Tokens are identified by **dot-separated string paths** (`color.primary`,
513:   `font.body.size`, `space.2`), case-sensitive, lowercase recommended. The
514:   `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type (`0x08`) references a token path stored in the
515:   arena; `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides a token's value globally.
516: - **Base = light. `dark.`-prefixed paths are the dark variant** (`dark.color.primary`).
517:   The renderer derives the effective scheme (light/dark) from the platform and
518:   re-resolves when it changes — scheme selection is never carried by the
519:   protocol.
520: - The **standard token catalog** (colors, typography, spacing, radii,
521:   elevations, `control.*`, per-component tokens) and the **resolution
522:   algorithm** (dark layer → override → default → parent → fallback) are defined
523:   in **[TOKENS.md](./TOKENS.md)**.
524: 
525: ### References in properties
526: 
527: Any property whose value type is `COLOR` / `F32` / `STRING` / `ENUM` MAY instead
528: carry the **`DESIGN_TOKEN`** value type (`0x08`), with `C` = arenaRef to the
529: token path. The renderer resolves the reference against the token tables and the
530: current scheme. A property carries exactly one value — a literal or a token
531: reference, never both. Because overrides and the scheme are renderer state, a
532: token-typed property requires **no re-emission** when a token changes.
533: 
534: ### Renderer Responsibilities
535: 
536: The renderer MUST:
537: 
538: 1. Provide platform-appropriate **light and dark defaults** for all Tier 1 tokens.
539: 2. Accept `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` commands and store overrides.
540: 3. Derive the effective color scheme from the platform and re-resolve on change.
541: 4. Resolve token references (`DESIGN_TOKEN` value type) in properties.
542: 5. Fall back to defaults when no override exists.
543: 6. Never transmit visual styling rules in the protocol.
544: 
545: The application MAY override any token via `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` (base and `dark.*`)
546: and reference tokens via the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type; it MUST NOT assume
547: specific default token values. Tokens a renderer cannot apply are ignored (the
548: same "allowed and ignored" rule as unapplicable modifiers).
549: 
550: ---
551: 
552: ## Frame Lifecycle
553: 
554: A frame is a batch of delta opcodes produced by one `emit` pass:
555: 
556: 1. Guest begins a frame.
557: 2. Guest emits the delta opcodes (tree structure and/or property changes) into consecutive ring slots.
558: 3. Guest allocates strings in the arena as needed.
559: 4. Guest `end_frame()`: publishes `writeCursor`, then increments `frameCount`.

- **Defaults = GTK-native**: resolve Tier-1 tokens at runtime via `StyleContext::lookup_color` of `@theme_*` names (`color.background`→`@theme_bg_color`, `color.surface`→`@theme_base_color`, `color.text.primary`→`@theme_fg_color`, `color.accent`/`color.primary`→`@theme_selected_bg_color`, `color.border`→`@borders`, `color.success/warning/danger`→`@success_color`/`@warning_color`/`@error_color`, …); **fall back to concrete HTML-style defaults** when no display/theme (keeps headless tests deterministic). Uses `pathland_core::tokens` resolution.
- **Scheme**: `gtk::Settings` → `gtk_application_prefer_dark_theme()` + `connect_gtk_application_prefer_dark_theme_notify`; on change, re-resolve + full `sync()`.

  `EventControllerMotion` (`EVENT_LISTENERS`-driven), plus **value/text events**
  (`VALUE_CHANGED` from toggle/slider/picker, `TEXT_CHANGED` from text field)
  **gated by `BINDING_ID`** (transport-aware event guards), sent through the
  two-way event arena.
- **Design tokens / theming (spec/TOKENS.md renderer contract)**:
  - `STYLE::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides are stored (`host.rs`), base + `dark.*`
    split by path prefix; STRING-valued overrides resolve the value string from
    the arena.
  - `DESIGN_TOKEN`-typed `SET_PROPERTY` values record the token path
    (`HostNode::token_refs`) and **resolve at apply time** against the theme,
    the active scheme, and the parent-fallback chain into concrete
    `properties`/`strings` (`RenderTree::resolve_tokens`, reusing
    `pathland_core::tokens`).
  - **Tier-1 default tables** (light + dark) in `host.rs`
    (`concrete_default_tables`) — concrete platform-appropriate fallbacks,
    **enriched with GTK-native theme colors** (`tokens.rs`:
    `StyleContext::lookup_color` of `@theme_*`/`@borders`/`@success_color`…)
    from the first widget's style context (headless → concrete fallback).
  - **Scheme detection** from the native GTK variant
    (`gtk::Settings` `prefer-dark` + `-dark` theme name); a notify handler
    calls `GtkRenderer::set_scheme`, which re-enriches native defaults and
    re-resolves + re-applies every token-referencing widget. Scheme is never
    carried by the protocol.
  - The generative `space.<N>` family resolves `space.base` × N.
  - Since GTK CSS has no custom properties, tokens resolve to **concrete**
    values (rgba/px/Pango) before the existing CSS-provider / text-style paths.

All six items are implemented and verified. Summary:

**1. Conformance vectors enforced**
- `pathland-core/src/conformance.rs`: vectors 17–18 (SET_DESIGN_TOKEN, DESIGN_TOKEN-typed SET_PROPERTY) + a ring test proving `Guest::set_design_token` emits vector 17 byte-exactly; new `pathland_core::tokens` module (no_std+alloc) with the reference resolution algorithm + the full CONFORMANCE resolution table tested.
- `pathland-core-transport`: vector 19 (network batch) byte-exact.
- Java: golden-byte opcode tests for 17/18 + `FrameCodec` DESIGN_TOKEN round-trip.

**2. HTML renderer Tier-1 defaults** — `--pl-space-base` (light+dark), canonical `font.body.*`, `control.*`/`button.*`/`input.*` catalog, radius scale, `border.width.thin`, `elevation.*` shadows; `.pathland-*` rules now reference canonical vars (focus ring → `control.accent`). Tests added.

**3. DSL theme helpers** — Rust `pathland_engine::Theme` + `Engine::apply_theme` (re-exported from `pathland-view`); Java `Theme` + `OpcodeSink.setDesignToken` in both sinks.

**4. STRING-valued token overrides** — `Guest::set_design_token_string`, spec vector 20, HTML renderer (quoted CSS), JS DOM `applyDesignToken`, and the Theme DSLs — all end-to-end.

Good idea — that's a cleaner ergonomic. Here's what it looks like today and the plan.

## Current API (`Theme.java`)
```java
.color("color.primary", 0xFF2563EB)      // base (light) only
.darkColor("color.primary", 0xFF60A5FA)  // dark variant in a separate call
```

## Proposed
Add a 3-arg overload — 1 color = light only, 2 colors = light + dark:
```java
.color("color.primary", 0xFF2563EB)                       // light only
.color("color.primary", 0xFF2563EB, 0xFF60A5FA)           // light + dark
```

Implementation is trivial — the 3-arg form pushes two overrides (base + `dark.`-prefixed), reusing the existing `dark(path)` helper:
```java
public Theme color(String path, int argb, int darkArgb) {
    return push(path, ValueTypes.COLOR, Color.of(argb))
            .push(dark(path), ValueTypes.COLOR, Color.of(darkArgb));
}
```

**Files touched:** `Theme.java` (new overload + Javadoc example), `EmitterTest.themeEmitsGlobalDesignTokenOverrides` (switch to the 2-color form + assert it emits both base and dark), `DemoTheme.java` (rewrite with the 2-color form), and the `Theme` bullet in `pathland-view/status.md`.

## Two design decisions I need from you

options.label: Remove them

options.label: Color only (Recommended)
options.description: Dark variants are overwhelmingly a color concern; keep f32/string using darkF32/darkString. Smallest, least-surprising change.

options.label: Extend to all builders
options.description: Add f32(path, light, dark) and string(path, light, dark) overloads too, for full symmetry (dark.space.base and dark.font.body.family are valid per spec).

22:   path) emit as `SET_PROPERTY` with the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type; unchanged
23:   refs reuse their arena offset across passes — **steady-state emission stays

content.text:
Root cause confirmed. This is a clean, small fix.

## The bug

`pathland-render-html/src/lib.rs:782` (`render_document`):
```rust
"{}{}\n</head>…", css::STYLE, tokens.css()
```
- `css::STYLE` is a complete `<style>…</style>` element.
- `tokens.css()` returns **bare rules** — `:root{--pl-color-primary:…}` and `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark){…}`.

So the SSR document emits:
```html
<style>…built-in design system…</style>
:root{--pl-color-primary:…}@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark){…}
</head>
```
The token rules sit between `</style>` and `</head>` as raw text — **outside any `<style>` element** — so the browser never applies them (the parser moves that text into `<body>`; overrides silently do nothing). Existing tests pass because they only assert substring presence (`html.contains(":root{…}")`), not placement.

The Java `pathland-render-html` shim delegates to this Rust renderer, so one fix covers both.

## The fix (`render_document`)

Wrap the rules in their own `<style data-pathland-tokens>` element, emitted **after** the built-in block (so the override `:root` variables win the cascade — same specificity, later wins) and matching the JS DOM client's `style[data-pathland-tokens]` element for symmetry:

```rust
let token_rules = tokens.css();
let token_style = if token_rules.is_empty() {
    String::new()                       // no overrides → no empty element
} else {
    format!("<style data-pathland-tokens>{token_rules}</style>\n")
};
// … {}{} → css::STYLE, token_style
```

Result:
```html
<style>…built-in…</style>
<style data-pathland-tokens>:root{…}@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark){…}</style>
</head>
```

## Tests & status

- **New test** in `lib.rs`: `design_token_css_renders_inside_a_style_element` — with `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` opcodes (base + dark + STRING), assert:
  - `html.contains("<style data-pathland-tokens>:root{--pl-color-primary:rgba(37,99,235,1);}")`
  - the `@media` dark rules are inside the same element (`…rgba(96,165,250,1);}}@media …` before `</style>`), and that `</style>@media` never appears (no bare rules after a style close)
  - a document with **no** overrides emits **no** `data-pathland-tokens` element.
- Existing `set_design_token_*` tests keep passing (substring assertions unaffected); `document_head_loads_inter_from_the_rsms_cdn` still finds the first `<style>`.
- `pathland-render-html/status.md` — note overrides render inside `<style data-pathland-tokens>` after the built-in block.

## Verification
- `cargo test -p pathland-render-html`
- Optional eyeball: `cd lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo && mvn quarkus:dev` → SSR HTML has the token `<style>` in `<head>`; toggle `prefers-color-scheme` and confirm re-theme works.

No wire change; `render_fragment` untouched (it embeds into a document that already defines the token variables). Ready to implement on approval.

**Bug**: `render_document` appended `tokens.css()` — bare `:root{…}` / `@media …` rules — directly after the built-in `</style>`, so the token overrides sat outside any `<style>` element and were never applied by the browser.

No overrides → no empty element (skipped via `tokens.css().is_empty()`).

**Test added**: `design_token_css_renders_inside_a_style_element` — asserts the base rule is inside the token style element, the element is closed after the dark media query, no bare rules appear after any `</style>`, and a document without overrides emits no `data-pathland-tokens` element.
